Why Does Seborrheic Dermatitis Happen?
It’s not just a surface issue; it’s a combination of factors:

Yeast Overgrowth: An overgrowth of natural yeast on the skin.

Inflammatory Reaction: Triggered in highly sensitive areas.

Barrier Disruption: A compromised skin barrier, which is often worsened by winter weather, harsh shampoos, and hot showers.

Where Else Can It Occur?
While most common on the scalp, Seborrheic Dermatitis can also show up on other parts of the body with redness, flaking, and itching:

Eyebrows & eyelashes

Around the nose

Beard area

Behind the ears

Upper chest

Dandruff vs. Seborrheic Dermatitis
Unlike regular dry dandruff, Seborrheic Dermatitis flakes are typically yellowish, greasy, and sit on top of red, inflamed skin. Remember: it’s a skin barrier and yeast problem, not just a flaking problem!
